fields.event: [SUMMARY] Radar contact at 10,000 yards on 12-plus ship convoy. Tracked on port flank, crossed ahead to right flank; dark conditions prevented sighting escorts or ships.

records.title: Narrative entry

fields.event: [SUMMARY] Approached starboard beam, broke off when convoy zigged and two more escorts appeared. Made several false starts over next half hour due to zigs and escorts.

records.title: Narrative entry

fields.event: One hit in the bow of #1 FREIGHTER, 60 seconds after firing. A large column of spray and smoke enveloped his forward part. He was last seen down by the bow, definitely sinking.

flags: Target typed as '⟦#⟧ 1 FREIGHTER'.
No position in the report. Placed on the track between the recorded positions at 1943-11-01 13:00 and 1943-11-01 16:45 GMT, as an estimate.

records.title: Narrative entry

fields.event: One hit amidships in #2 FREIGHTER, 90 seconds after firing. This was a terrific explosion. Smoke and debris rose over the tops of his masts, and continued to rise and spread until not only the remains of this ship, but also several other ships, were obscured. Smoke and poor visibility prevented seeing this one sink.

fields.event: [SUMMARY] Three hits; target disintegrated with bow broken off vertically and sinking immediately, and after two thirds remaining awash two minutes before sinking flat.
Ran through a large diesel oil slick. Heard indescribable screaming and yelling from ahead, and saw a group of two or three life boats and about five life rafts.
Reversed course and searched for survivors, but could find only one shattered empty life boat. Finally departed, course 160° T, at full speed.
No further contacts; dived. Rough weather and poor visibility throughout day (from 500 to 5000 yards) precluded any surface search.
Heard four distant explosions.
Surfaced, transmitted message on course 090° T, then came to 290° T at 16 knots.
[SUMMARY] Sighted life raft 25 yards away with three men; stopped abreast, but raft drifted away in darkness during maneuvers and could not be relocated.

Review: Ship contact 4 (periscope, SS submerged): checked on the scan. The table has 0306 Z 6 Nov (1206 I 6 November); the narrative has 1206 I 7 November. Same time of day, different date: one is a typing error in the report. The track favours the narrative: aircraft contact 5 puts the boat at 29-04 N 132-25 E at 0636 I on 6 November, about 95 miles east of this position, and she dived at 0636; reaching 130-38 E by 1206 would need about 17 knots, mostly submerged. fields.description: 10,000 ton transport, coal burner, composite 3 deck super- structure, about 1/4 length of ship. Single raked stack, raked bow, cruiser stern. Lightly loaded, much deck cargo, two shallow wells, four pairs of goal posts, two forward, two aft. AIKOKU MARU, page 43 of ONI 208-J most nearly approximates this ship in appearance.
fields.damage determined by: Saw two torpedoes hit. Saw ships picking up survivors. Passed through debris consisting of lifeboats, rafts, section of bridge, and shattered hatch covers, etc.
